result:
Only Solution 1 reaches the correct answer, t* = 2π/p.

The graph Cay(ℤ_{2p}, ℤ_{2p}^×) joins x and y exactly when y−x is odd and not divisible by p. It is therefore K_{p,p} minus the perfect matching x ~ x+p. Its eigenvalues are p−1 (once), −(p−1) (once), 1 (p−1 times) and −1 (p−1 times). These are the Ramanujan sums that Solution 1 lists.

Solution 1's amplitudes follow from this spectrum. For d ≠ 0, p, the amplitude U(t)_{0,d} contains the factor sin(pt/2) times either cos((p−2)t/2) (d odd) or sin((p−2)t/2) (d even). Both parities occur for p ≥ 3, for example d = 1 and d = 2. The cosine and sine cannot vanish together, so fractional revival between 0 and p needs sin(pt/2) = 0, i.e. t = 2πm/p. At those times U e₀ = cos t e₀ + i sin t e_p. This is a genuine fractional revival when p ∤ m. The smallest such time is 2π/p. The p = 3 check on C₆ also agrees.

Solution 2 gives p, which is not supported by any spectral calculation and is wrong. Solution 3 gives 2π/(p−1). That is only the time at which the phase of the eigenvalue p−1 returns to 1. Revival of the walk depends on all four eigenvalues, so this is wrong.

VERDICT 1: ACCEPT
VERDICT 2: REJECT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
